status: Isolated Chat history and professional web shell loading gates removed and verified.
changes: Chat releases its loading view as soon as signed/authorized history is published, allowing messages to render while reactions, message status, saved IDs and starred IDs load.
The four independent Chat decorations start together instead of waiting for reactions before dispatching the other three reads.
Stale Chat metadata is rejected before dispatching media signing. Existing generation/conversation checks continue to protect publication and final loading/error state.

The professional web AppShell returns after authenticated viewer resolution without issuing a navigation-profile query whose result it never uses. Standard navigation still waits for and renders that profile.

ChatScreen.baselineComparison: Same rule/message multiset as HEAD; no warning suppressions added.

observations: With every Chat enrichment promise deliberately held, production fetchMessages has published one authorized message, historyLoaded=true and loading=false, while all four enrichment reads have started.
With Chat signing held or rejected, no message publication or enrichment is permitted. Conversation/account/unmount and later-request races do not publish stale state.
The actual AppShell async function returns the professional workspace with call, media-lightbox and scroll layers present and zero profile query dispatches.
Pending authentication still prevents AppShell resolution, and the signed-out shell remains signed out. Ordinary navigation still waits for its own profile read.
limits: The Chat tests execute extracted production screen callbacks with controlled state and transport, plus existing call/media authorization regressions. They do not measure native pixel continuity, network latency or device performance.
AppShell is executed as an actual transpiled async React component using mocked viewer/database and child components. This proves the removed query dependency, not deployed Next route latency.
Private media authorization remains on the Chat display path. No new private message cache or authorization bypass was introduced.
ChatScreen retains 20 pre-existing lint warnings unrelated to the changed callback; this evidence does not claim the whole file or app is lint-clean.
